en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for having the most perfect volcanic cone shape in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the sea.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and provides most of the region's hydroelectric power.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle is the national bird and is found only in the forests of Mindanao.
The Philippines is the top global producer of abaca, a banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes and currency.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro is scientifically recognized as the center of global marine shorefish biodiversity.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera region were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over two millennia ago.
The tamaraw is a small, endangered hoofed mammal related to the water buffalo that is found exclusively on Mindoro island.
